# OSS KB Update Proposal: PyPI PyJWT (`pyjwt`)

## Package Overview

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Ecosystem** | PyPI |
| **Package** | `pyjwt` |
| **PURL** | `pkg:pypi/pyjwt` |
| **Latest Version** | 2.12.1 |
| **Repository** | https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt |
| **Popularity** | ~584M downloads/month (extremely high adoption) |

---

## Vulnerability Inventory (4 advisories)

### 1. GHSA-752w-5fwx-jx9f — Unknown `crit` header extensions accepted

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-32597 |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Introduced** | 0 (all versions) |
| **Fixed** | 2.12.0 |
| **Last known affected** | ≤ 2.11.0 |
| **Summary** | PyJWT did not validate the `crit` (critical) JOSE header parameter, allowing tokens with unknown critical extensions to be accepted without verification, potentially bypassing security controls. |
| **Changelog** | "2.12.0 validates crit header via GHSA-752w-5fwx-jx9f" ✔ confirmed |

### 2. GHSA-75c5-xw7c-p5pm — Issuer (`iss`) partial-match bypass

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **CVE** | CVE-2024-53861 |
| **Severity** | LOW |
| **Introduced** | 2.10.0 |
| **Fixed** | 2.10.1 |
| **Summary** | The issuer validation logic allowed partial string matches (e.g., `iss="example"` would match `"example.com"`), enabling potential issuer spoofing. Narrow affected window (single version). |
| **Changelog** | "2.10.1 prevents partial iss matching via GHSA-75c5-xw7c-p5pm" ✔ confirmed |

### 3. GHSA-ffqj-6fqr-9h24 — Key confusion via non-blocklisted public key formats

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **CVE** | CVE-2022-29217 |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Introduced** | 1.5.0 |
| **Fixed** | 2.4.0 |
| **Summary** | Asymmetric key material in non-blocklisted PEM formats (e.g., SSH, X.509 certificate) could be used as HMAC secrets, enabling algorithm confusion / key-confusion attacks. |
| **Changelog** | "2.4.0 security entry CVE-2022-29217 key confusion" ✔ confirmed |

> **⚠ Duplicate alias flag:** This advisory carries alias `PYSEC-2022-202` in addition to the CVE. Ensure KB deduplicates GHSA-ffqj-6fqr-9h24 / CVE-2022-29217 / PYSEC-2022-202 as a single record.

### 4. GHSA-r9jw-mwhq-wp62 — Original key confusion (PKCS#1 PEM)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **CVE** | CVE-2017-11424 |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Introduced** | 0 (all versions) |
| **Fixed** | 1.5.1 |
| **Summary** | PKCS#1-formatted PEM public keys were not rejected when used with HMAC algorithms, enabling algorithm-confusion attacks where an attacker signs a token with a known public key. |
| **Changelog** | "1.5.1 guarded against PKCS1 PEM public keys PR #277" ✔ confirmed |

> **⚠ Duplicate alias flag:** This advisory carries alias `PYSEC-2017-24` alongside the CVE. Ensure KB deduplicates GHSA-r9jw-mwhq-wp62 / CVE-2017-11424 / PYSEC-2017-24 as a single record.

---

## Thematic Analysis

| Theme | Advisories | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Algorithm / key confusion** | CVE-2017-11424, CVE-2022-29217 | Recurring pattern spanning 5 years. The 2022 fix addressed formats missed by the 2017 fix. Both HIGH severity. |
| **Claim validation logic** | CVE-2024-53861 | Introduced and fixed within the 2.10.x series; regression-type issue. |
